title: Unified contact-free formulation of linear-response transport theory
abstract: Thermal Hall transport is conventionally formulated as a current--current Kubo response supplemented by an energy-magnetization correction obtained through an auxiliary pseudogravitational magnetic field. Motivated by this structure, we develop a unified contact-free moment formulation of linear response to scalar sources. For channels whose source contributions vanish in the dc limit, the transport coefficient is the low-frequency residue of a retarded moment--moment correlator, with equal-time endpoint contributions incorporated before the dc limit is taken. The formulation uses only scalar sources, requires no separate magnetization subtraction, is independent of the local-current gauge, and is invariant under admissible redistributions of bond or interaction energy. It organizes particle, grand-energy, and specified spin-density channels within a common source--moment response matrix. Quadratic Landau--Lifshitz spin waves illustrate the method: the secular growth of polarization-moment correlations isolates the finite Hall residue and yields the magnon thermal Hall and spin Nernst coefficients from the same paraunitary band geometry. The formulation provides a unified operator framework that simplifies the organization of particle, thermal, and spin transport and can streamline calculations by eliminating separate contact and magnetization corrections.
summary: This paper introduces a unified, contact-free theoretical framework for calculating linear-response transport coefficients in quantum systems. By reformulating the problem using a common source-moment response matrix, it elegantly bypasses traditional difficulties associated with magnetization corrections and gauge dependence. This provides a powerful, streamlined tool for calculating complex transport phenomena like the thermal Hall effect.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a unified, contact-free formulation for linear-response transport theory, particularly for thermal and spin transport coefficients.
main_result: The new formulation organizes particle, grand-energy, and spin-density channels into a common source-moment response matrix, eliminating the need for separate magnetization subtractions and gauge dependence.
method: It employs a moment formulation derived from the Kubo linear-response theory, using finite-q regulators to handle periodic boundary conditions and systematically taking the low-frequency limit.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to general quantum transport problems, exemplified by analyzing spin-wave excitations in a Heisenberg ferromagnet. The framework utilizes a grand Hamiltonian density and associated continuity equations.
key_observables: Thermal Hall coefficient ($\kappa$), spin Nernst coefficient ($\alpha_s$), and general transport coefficients derived from moment-moment correlators.
important_parameters: Low-frequency limit ($\omega 	o 0$), DC limit, and the structure of the source-moment response matrix.
main_assumptions: The formulation assumes that source contributions vanish in the dc limit for the simplest derivation, and the spin-wave example assumes a conserved longitudinal spin component.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes focus on mathematical derivations and conceptual framework rather than figure descriptions).
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general theory of linear response, addressing ambiguities in current definition and gauge freedom. It introduces the unified moment formulation, derives the contact-free Kubo formula, and then applies this framework to calculate specific coefficients like the thermal Hall and spin Nernst effects using spin-wave models.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework for handling gauge ambiguities and separating different energy/spin contributions in transport coefficients is highly valuable for any theorist working on non-equilibrium quantum dynamics or open quantum systems where current definitions are subtle.
